audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer calls this FAVOURED, difficulty 4/10, carry threat 5/10, with the level chart showing Mel ahead from level 1 through 2+ items. The content layer's chart and the packet both give Mordekaiser levels 2 through first item, and the matchup sits at 26.67% over 15 games.
audit.why: The two layers contradict each other and the full layer contradicts the win rate. A player reading the full-layer chart is being told to step up during exactly the levels the data says he kills them.
audit.corrected: HARD, difficulty 8/10, carry threat 8/10; phases Skill / Mordekaiser x5 / Skill, matching the content layer.
sources: scratchpad packet mel.json entry mordekaiser (winRate 26.67, games 15, levelChart)

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers lean on Rebuttal's reflect: the full tldr says 'you reflect what he throws' and content wants.you[1] said 'Hold W to reflect or eat his E'. Death's Grasp is described by Riot as 'Mordekaiser pulls all enemies in an area' — not a projectile.
audit.why: Mordekaiser's kit is projectile-free end to end: Obliterate is a 675-range ground slam, Indestructible is self-cast, Death's Grasp is an area pull, Realm of Death is point-blank at 650. Rebuttal's reflect clause never fires in this matchup, so telling a Mel to hold W as the answer to the pull gets her killed holding a button that does nothing to it.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal is a damage blank and a move-speed tool here, nothing more. The answer to Death's Grasp is standing past 700, not W.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mordekaiser.json — no projectile flag on any slot

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions that Obliterate's damage is increased when it hits a single enemy.
audit.why: Riot's own text: 'Damage is increased when hitting a single enemy.' For a 550-range mage with no dash, deliberately standing inside her own minion wave is a free reduction on his primary trade tool — and it is the opposite of the instinct to step out and poke cleanly.
audit.corrected: Never trade away from your own wave; Obliterate hits harder on an isolated target, so standing in the minions is a damage cut.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer's level-6 phase said 'Golden Eclipse online — anyone you've stacked is now walking around with a countdown', framing 6 as Mel's spike.
audit.why: Level 6 is Mordekaiser's spike, not Mel's: Realm of Death is a 650-range point-blank banish that removes every ally and every escape route from the equation, and Mel's only defensive layer does not stop it. The content layer already says this correctly; the full layer said the reverse.
audit.corrected: Level 6 rewritten around Realm of Death's 650 range and 140s cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers at all — 'track it always. Count it out loud if you must.'
audit.why: The windows here are numeric and decisive: Realm of Death 140/120/100, Death's Grasp 16/14/12/10/8 at 700 range, Indestructible 12/11/10/9/8. Surviving one ult at rank 1 buys more than two minutes of a safe lane; that is the biggest tempo fact in the matchup and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real cooldowns and the 650/700 range bands.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer itemization line says 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain', but nothing anywhere explains what it is for or when it matters.
audit.why: Indestructible stores damage dealt and taken and converts it into a heal on an 8-12s cooldown. A poke mage's chip is precisely the input that fills it, so Grievous Wounds is not a luxury purchase here — without it the entire poke plan feeds his sustain.
audit.corrected: Tied Grievous Wounds to Indestructible's 12s cycle in phases[5].why and the content mid text.

edits.before: Level 1 is a real fight — your ranged auto and one ability out-range his melee Q, and his W shield is the only thing keeping him healthy, so chip him and don't overstay. The trap is Level 2-3: you get Q and Solar Snare and want to root-and-poke, but his E pull cancels your spacing the second the root ends, and his W shield absorbs the Q chunk you were counting on. Don't throw a greedy E from up close — if you root him he just walks the slow field and W-heals it back, and now he's in pull range.
edits.after: Level 1 is a real fight — your ranged auto and Radiant Volley out-range his 675-range Obliterate, and Indestructible is the only thing keeping him healthy, so chip him and don't overstay. The trap is Level 2-3: you get Q and Solar Snare and want to root-and-poke, but Death's Grasp reaches 700 and cancels your spacing the second the root ends. Obliterate also deals bonus damage to an isolated target, so never step away from your own wave to trade — standing in your minions is a straight damage cut.

edits.before: This is where it goes wrong, and it's why the lane is HARD. At 6 his Realm of Death takes you into a 1v1 box and steals your AP — your whole kit is poke-and-kite and there is no kiting inside that wall. He sustains your Q with W, eats your single root, and once he's on you his isolated Q does more than your entire poke chain. Save Solar Snare to peel his E or interrupt his walk-up, never to start a trade, and keep Flash exclusively for the moment his R drops you next to him.
edits.after: This is where it goes wrong, and it's why the lane is HARD. At 6 Realm of Death takes you into a 1v1 box from 650 range and steals your AP — there is no kiting inside that wall. It is a 140s cooldown at rank 1, so surviving one buys you two quiet minutes. Indestructible turns everything you chip him for into a heal every 12s, so bring Grievous Wounds before you commit to a poke war, and keep Flash exclusively for the moment his R drops you next to him.
